questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The indicator used during the estimation of $COD$ of a water sample is
questions.solution:
According to the question,& In environmental chemistry, the& chemical oxygen demand (COD) is an indicative measure of the amount of oxygen that can be consumed by reactions in a measured solution. It is commonly expressed in mass of oxygen consumed over volume of solution which in SI units is milligrams per litre (mg / L).

In the titration method for determining COD, the& excess dichromate is reacted with a reducing agent, ferrous ammonium sulphate. As the ferrous ammonium sulphate (FAS) is added slowly, the excess dichromate is converted into its trivalent form.

During the titration the ferroin is used as indicator. At the end point the colour of the ferroin changes from blue-green to a reddish brown. The consumption of the dichromate is proportional to the amount of organic matters that are present in the water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) is a measure of organic materials present in water, BOD value less than $5 \mathrm{ppm}$ indicates a water sample to be
questions.solution:
The amount of oxygen required by bacteria to break down the organic matter present in a certain volume of a sample of water, is called biochemical oxygen demand (BOD).
The amount of BOD in the water is a measure of the amount of organic material in the water, in terms of much oxygen will be required to break it down biologically. Clean water would have BOD value of less than 5 ppm whereas highly polluted water could have a BOD value of 17 ppm or more. It means BOD value less than $5 \mathrm{ppm}$ indicates a water sample to be rich in dissolved oxygen.

questions.q:
Consider the following reactions involving some atmospheric pollutants.
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{NO}+\mathrm{O}_3 \rightarrow \mathrm{NO}_2+\mathrm{O}_2 \xrightarrow{h \nu} \mathrm{NO}+\mathrm{O}_3 \\
& 4 \mathrm{NO}_2+\mathrm{O}_2+2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \longrightarrow 4 \mathrm{HNO}_3 \\
& 3 \mathrm{CH}_4+2 \mathrm{O}_3 \longrightarrow 3 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}+3 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}
\end{aligned}$
Based on the above, the formation of formaldehyde from methane in the atmosphere will be controlled by
questions.solution:
Following reaction involving some atmospheric pollutants :
$\begin{array}{r}
\mathrm{NO}+\mathrm{O}_3 \longrightarrow \mathrm{NO}_2+\mathrm{O}_2 \xrightarrow{h \nu} \mathrm{NO}+\mathrm{O}_3 \\
4 \mathrm{NO}_2+\mathrm{O}_2+2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \longrightarrow 4 \mathrm{HNO}_3 \\
3 \mathrm{CH}_4+2 \mathrm{O}_3 \longrightarrow 3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{O}+3 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}
\end{array}$
The formation of formaldehyde $\left(\mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)$ from methane $\left(\mathrm{CH}_4\right)$ in the atmosphere will be controlled by $\mathrm{O}_3, \mathrm{NO}$ and $\mathrm{NO}_2$. Hence, option (3) is correct.

$\mathrm{Ca}_{10}\left(\mathrm{PO}_4\right)_6 \mathrm{ F}_2$ can be rewritten as :
$3 \left[\m$mathrm{Ca}_3$\left(\mathrm{PO}}_{4}\right)$_2\right]$\mathrm{CaF}}_{2} \text{ or }3 \left[\mathrm{Ca}}_{3} \left(\mathrm{PO}_4\right)_2 \cdot \mathrm{CaF}_2\right]$
Hence, option (4) is the correct answer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among the following compounds, which one is not responsible for depletion of ozone layer?
questions.solution:
In stratosphere the following reactions takes place which are responsible for depletion of ozone layer.
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{NO}+\mathrm{O}_3 \longrightarrow \mathrm{NO}_2+\mathrm{O}_2 \\ & \mathrm{CF}_2 \mathrm{Cl}_2 \stackrel{h v}{\longrightarrow} \dot{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{F}_2 \mathrm{Cl}+\dot{\mathrm{Cl}} \\ & \mathrm{CFCl}_3 \stackrel{h v}{\longrightarrow} \dot{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{FCl}_2+\dot{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{l} \\ & \dot{\mathrm{C}} 1+\mathrm{O}_3 \longrightarrow \mathrm{Cl} \dot{\mathrm{O}}+\mathrm{O}_2 \\ & \mathrm{Cl} \dot{\mathrm{O}}+\mathrm{O} \longrightarrow \dot{\mathrm{C}}+\mathrm{O}_2 \\ & \end{aligned}$
Hence, methane $\left(\mathrm{CH}_4\right)$ is not responsible for ozone layer depletion.
questions.question: Among the following compounds, which one is not responsible for depletion of ozone layer?
questions.explanation:
In stratosphere the following reactions takes place which are responsible for depletion of ozone layer.
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{NO}+\mathrm{O}_3 \longrightarrow \mathrm{NO}_2+\mathrm{O}_2 \\ & \mathrm{CF}_2 \mathrm{Cl}_2 \stackrel{h v}{\longrightarrow} \dot{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{F}_2 \mathrm{Cl}+\dot{\mathrm{Cl}} \\ & \mathrm{CFCl}_3 \stackrel{h v}{\longrightarrow} \dot{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{FCl}_2+\dot{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{l} \\ & \dot{\mathrm{C}} 1+\mathrm{O}_3 \longrightarrow \mathrm{Cl} \dot{\mathrm{O}}+\mathrm{O}_2 \\ & \mathrm{Cl} \dot{\mathrm{O}}+\mathrm{O} \longrightarrow \dot{\mathrm{C}}+\mathrm{O}_2 \\ & \end{aligned}$
Hence, methane $\left(\mathrm{CH}_4\right)$ is not responsible for ozone layer depletion.
